newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia frees most detainees after Timor clash.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia frees most detainees after Timor clash.

text.p: Indonesian police in East Timor said on Monday they had freed 105 of 109 youths detained after brawls between Catholics and members of an army-backed youth group early this month, the official Antara news agency said.

"There now remains only four perpetrators of the damage who are still being questioned and who are suspected of being the cause of that incident," East Timor police chief Colonel Jusuf Muharam was quoted as saying in Dili, the territory's main city, on Monday.
Muharam said the seriousness of the incident should not be exaggerated as it was not related to politics and could be categorised as a purely criminal matter.

East Timor military commander Colonel Mahidin Simbolon denied reports over the weekend that six people had been killed during the fighting between February 7 and 9 in Viqueque, about 100 km (60 miles) east of Dili.
"It is totally untrue the reports saying that six people have been killed in the clash... It is not true, nobody has died," Simbolon was quoted by Antara as saying on Saturday.
Simbolon, who spoke in Dili, capital of the former Portuguese territory, also denied reports that a number of Catholic priests had been beaten during the brawls.
Church sources have said fights broke out after members of the military-backed Gada Paksi youth organisation attacked 10 Catholic youths, a priest and his driver on February 7.
Gada Paksi, or Youth Guard of Integration Upholders, was set up in 1995 and its members receive military-style training on Indonesia's main island of Java.
East Timorese residents have accused members of the group of intimidating people who oppose the territory's integration with Indonesia.

Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony in 1975 and annexed it a year later, a move not recognised by the United Nations. Simmering tension between local residents and Indonesian security forces sent to the island has occasionally erupted in violence over the years.
